reviews.decision_reason: select_demand keeps the full selected data path from the supplied corpus: the function selects all records with demand_score >= 3 while also preserving explicit fallback identifiers. In this package all eight corpus records satisfy the threshold, so this boundary does not localize the one-row truncation seen downstream.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: preserve selected records and fallback identifiers
avoid unsupported market-demand expansion beyond supplied corpus

reviews.decision_reason: normalize is the behaviorally significant fault. Its declared role is to produce a bounded normalized needs DataFrame preserving allowed corpus identifiers, but the implementation hard-codes index_window = [0] and returns retained_df.head(len(index_window)), reducing the eight selected/retained records to one. That causes only n06-r01 to survive into needs and evidence_sources, hiding other supplied demand records and making missing/contradictory demand evidence invisible.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: preserve allowed corpus identifiers after normalization
keep missing or contradictory demand evidence visible
produce bounded normalized needs without unrelated candidates

reviews.decision_reason: assemble_provenance deterministically ranks and emits provenance for the rows it receives. The inspected output contains the expected one-row provenance shape for n06-r01, but that one-row input was already truncated by normalize, so any incomplete provenance is downstream of the failed normalization boundary rather than localized here.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: assemble ranked source provenance with deterministic ordering
preserve two exact handoff artifacts for downstream job
